notes: The full source is 2369 × 1686 pixels. The provided halves are overlapping left and right images of 1244 × 1686 and 1245 × 1686 pixels. Whole, a, b were each viewed once before any crop.

This is one handwritten sheet with sketches concentrated in the upper-left, a corrected category-name row below, and two further mathematical lines. Much of the right side is blank. No title, date, prose paragraph, typewriting, printed reused sheet text, or manuscript folio was found.
The lower-left 1 is treated as an archive sheet number, not as an author folio. It is present in a LaTeX comment.

The sketches juxtapose subdivided segments, one-dimensional strips, hatched lobes, a double lobe and a four-cell frame. Calling these cell complexes is an interpretation used by H, not manuscript prose. No theorem is stated or checked here.

The category row has corrections at the third and last names and heavy retracing in the second connector. The replacement Maquettes is visibly above struck Triang. H expands that abbreviation without support from the ink.
No explicit verbal author doubt, date, title, or question was read. Uncertainty in this report concerns overlapping strokes and the origin of nonlinguistic marks, not an author-written question.
The first lens central ink cannot be assigned a defensible word count. The reading traces it and removes the editorial one-word illegibility node. Whether a cancelled word lies beneath is unresolved.
The initial F forms are read as capitals; x and y are baseline arguments. The source itself does not explain F. No mathematical background claim was required to settle the glyphs.

All C TikZ groups, dots, cell counts, internal dividers, contour gaps and hatching strokes were checked against the source. The first lens upper-left gap was restored; its central scribble was retraced without a textual label; the lower-right marks were added.

H_drawing.tex was read only after the parent clarified that this page-specific witness was permitted. No other page, full H batch, other reader file, OCR, recognition system, web source or published parallel was consulted.
